metadata.title: Which of Gardner's Eight Intelligences Can a Machine Do? (Short)
metadata.thesis: Gardner did ask which intelligences machines can do. By his own 2024 account six of eight rooms are lit, but under a performance test, not the 1983 one. The last two stay dark for reasons no test result supplies.
metadata.source_project: claude-for-design/introducing-theoristai (10-beat auto-conversion, Substack byline Humanitarians AI, March 2026; used as base topic, template discarded)

beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Tanmay Kulkarni, in for Humanitarians AI. An essay I read this week says that in nineteen eighty-three, technology "was not yet a serious competitor" to any of Howard Gardner's intelligences. So I went and read what Gardner wrote later. He did ask. And he answered, one intelligence at a time.

props.command: which of Gardner's intelligences can a machine do?
output: “not yet a serious competitor to any of them”

beats.narration_text: Think of his theory as a house with eight rooms. Words, logic, space, music, the body, nature, other people, and yourself. In October twenty twenty-four, he and two colleagues took machines through that house. A light only comes on where they say a machine does what the room is for.

props.heading: Gardner's house: eight rooms
props.source: Rooms: Gardner, Frames of Mind (1983) + naturalist (mid-1990s) · Gardner, Furuzawa & Stachura, ‘Who Owns Intelligence?’, MI Oasis, Oct 2024 · ‘Introducing Theorist.ai’, Humanitarians AI, March 2026

captionSteps.text: A light comes on only when Gardner's own writing says a machine does it.

beats.narration_text: Words and logic go first. Language models, they write, "clearly exhibit the signs" of both. Two lights. Space: on, and that one surprised me, because chess and Go are filed there, not under logic. Music: on, even new pieces in distinctive styles. The body, the room I'd have bet stayed dark: programs that "adroitly" handle objects. On. And nature: on. That's six.

props.heading: Gardner's house: eight rooms
props.source: Rooms: Gardner, Frames of Mind (1983) + naturalist (mid-1990s) · Gardner, Furuzawa & Stachura, ‘Who Owns Intelligence?’, MI Oasis, Oct 2024 · ‘Introducing Theorist.ai’, Humanitarians AI, March 2026

captionSteps.text: A light comes on only when Gardner's own writing says a machine does it.
LLMs “clearly exhibit the signs of high logical-mathematical and high linguistic intelligence”
Spatial: “Mastering games like chess or Go”
Musical: “creating credible new ones in distinctive styles”
Bodily-kinesthetic: “adroitly manipulating objects of various shapes and sizes”
Naturalist: grouping “human-created entities … from thimbles to airplanes”

beats.narration_text: Two rooms are left, the personal ones, and here the paper says "one should be more cautious." Other people, it leaves ajar: it lists diplomacy, salesmanship, therapeutic interactions. And knowing yourself stays dark. Using that word for a program at all, they write, "can be seen as a 'category error.'" So it isn't dark because a machine failed. It's dark because, on their reading, the question doesn't apply.

captionSteps.text: Naturalist: grouping “human-created entities … from thimbles to airplanes”
Personal intelligences: “one should be more cautious” · Interpersonal evidence: “diplomacy, salesmanship, gamesmanship, therapeutic interactions”
Intrapersonal: “can be seen as a ‘category error’”

interior.title: Room 8 · Intrapersonal
interior.caption: “can be seen as a ‘category error’”
interior.source: Gardner, Furuzawa & Stachura, ‘Who Owns Intelligence?’, MI Oasis, Oct 2024

beats.narration_text: So: six lights on, one door ajar, one room dark on purpose. And that essay's sentence? The same paper's history of the field puts programs doing logic and math back in nineteen fifty-six, before the house was even built. So one of those lights may have been on all along.

props.heading: Gardner's house: eight rooms
props.source: Rooms: Gardner, Frames of Mind (1983) + naturalist (mid-1990s) · Gardner, Furuzawa & Stachura, ‘Who Owns Intelligence?’, MI Oasis, Oct 2024 · ‘Introducing Theorist.ai’, Humanitarians AI, March 2026

captionSteps.text: Intrapersonal: “can be seen as a ‘category error’”
Six lights on · one door ajar · one room dark on purpose
Essay: in 1983, technology “was not yet a serious competitor to any of them” · Record: 1956 programs “carried out mathematical and logical operations”

beats.narration_text: The full video opens every door, and asks what it would take to switch on room seven. It's linked right below. Tanmay Kulkarni, in for Humanitarians AI.
